extracts.lead_summary: Diplacy did in five sessions what the Fed couldn't: it broke the breakout. WTI fell -$7.4 to $92.92 — through the $5 trigger line, Brent through $100 to $98.58 — after a three-hour U.S.-Iran meeting at UNGA opened the first real ceasefire window of the conflict (issue #116). XLE closed $62.04 (-3.5%), a weekly close below the $63.46 breakout line — failed breakout #2 by the letter of last week's map — saved from worse by the 50D ($61.66), which was tagged to the penny and held. The refiner mean-reversion ignited exactly where the warning said it would: MPC -7.4% from RSI 90, VLO -6.3%, PSX -6.4%. And the physical market files its dissent: VLCCs still earn $1.10M a day, the Houthis hold Mokha and Perim Island, France is deploying to Yanbu, and Aramco's October European cancellation stands. The price of oil is pricing peace. The market for moving oil is pricing war. One of them is wrong.
